opportunities.idea: War-booty arbitrage: buying loot from departing mercenaries and selling elsewhere, as a trade mechanic.

ledger.summary: A company of about forty (some ten men-at-arms, about six merchants and servants with pack animals) crosses the ford and passes Ralph; among them are his brother Blaise and Richard the Red. Blaise has become a prosperous merchant, having bought loot cheaply from Companions who had taken a town and traded from town to town. He is bound for Whitwall, a great market. Ralph tells his adventures but not of the Lady. They reach Whitwall by evening: a great, well-defended town with high new walls, and lodge at the chapmen's hostel.
ledger.geography_notes: Whitwall lies within an afternoon and evening's ride of the Swelling Flood ford, on the same side as Ralph (crossing back would be the "backward way"). The merchants came through the wildwoods to reach it.
open_questions: Which town did the Companions take and sell to Blaise?
